exact_statement: Determine how large n must be as a function of r >= 2 so that there is an antichain in 2^[n] occupying n-3 distinct ranks and containing at least r members on every occupied rank.
scope_notes: Round nine proves the memberwise upper bound rho(j)<=2+ceil(log2(j+4)) on actual odd K4,r9 members.
Round ten prioritizes a matching explicit lower-bound subsequence, not another existence proof.
The candidate subsequence is j_R=11*2^(R-4)-5 for every R>=5; the target is the exact identity rho(j_R)=R+1.
An asymptotically sharp fixed-family recovery rate remains local. It does not give rank-42 recovery, cover all adjacent orbits, establish suffix persistence, or change the public Erdos-776 threshold.
